newsitem.title: UK: IPE June gas oil closes down on bearish U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: IPE June gas oil closes down on bearish U.S. data.

text.p: IPE June gas oil closed $2.50 down at $170.75 a tonne on Wednesday, but off the day's lows, pushed down by bearish U.S. weekly stock data, traders said.

The contract traded as high as $171.75 but also as low as $169.75 soon after NYMEX opened lower following the release of U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data showing crude stocks rose 6.4 million barrels and gasoline stocks were up 4.7 million barrels last week.

The DOE data confirmed American Petroleum Institute (API) figures issued late on Tuesday which said U.S. crude stocks rose 6.94 million barrels and gasoline stocks grew by 6.51 million barrels last week.
"Gas oil did not do much towards the close. It was very boring...but it was basically down because of the U.S. data," one broker said.

Meanwhile, June Brent was holding to its afternoon trading levels when it shed some of its earlier losses despite the bearish U.S. crude stocks data. June Brent was trading 27 cents a barrel down at $19.35 by 1702 GMT.
